Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 2.1 Start a Construction 2.2 Recruit a Worker 2.3 Make an Investment 2.4 Send a Worker to work 2.5 Take Coins 2.6 Completing a Building 3 End of the game Overview This is a wonderful strategic game where one’s goal is to use one’s workers to maximum capacity while building buildings which create both income & victory points for the player! In the end, whoever is able to obtain the most victory points is the winning player! Gameplay The game is played over a series of turns, until someone has reached 17 points. On your turn, you get to take 3 actions and additional actions, at the cost of 5 coins for each extra action. You may use actions to: Start a Construction Recruit a Worker Make an Investment Send a Worker to work Take Coins Start a Construction You take 1 Building from the five available Building cards and place it in front of you, at the cost of 1 action. Recruit a Worker You take 1 Worker from the five available Worker cards and place it in front of you, at the cost of 1 action. Make an Investment Once per turn, you can take one of the cards on the Investment line, at the cost of 1 action: purchase a prisoner : for 7 coins, you can take one of the slaves in the Investment line. The slave is considered as a Worker, but does not have to be paid when sent to work. At the cost of one action (or 5 coins at the end of the game), you can free them, but they now have to be paid when sent to work. Each slave makes you lose a victory point at the end of the game if not freed. A Slave cannot use a tool or be educated until freed. buy a tool : for 2 coins, you can take one of the tool cards on the Investment line. Whenever you send a Worker to work, you can equip them with the tool at no additional cost (no coin or action). take a loan : you can take a loan card from the Investment line, gaining 10 coins. However, at the end of the game, you must pay 15 coins for each taken loan, or lose 2 points per unpaid loan. Paying a loan isn't an action. educate a Worker : for 7 coins, you can take one of the clear education card on the Investment line and add it on top of one of your available Workers. The new resource level replaces the old one and the cost for sending this worker to work is not increased. An education card remains on the same worker until the end of the game. Send a Worker to work You place one of your Workers next to one of your buildings under construction. You must pay the coin cost indicated on the Worker card. That Worker is now tied to the Building until it is completed. Sending a worker has a cost of 1 action, except: if you send a second Worker, on the same turn , to the same Building , sending that 2nd Worker has a cost of 2 actions. if you send a third Worker, on the same turn , to the same Building , sending that 3rd Worker has a cost of 3 actions. etc... So if you send another Worker to a different Building, it only cost you a standard 1 action. Take Coins You can spend 1 action to get 1 coin, 2 actions to get 3 coins or 3 actions to get 6 coins. Completing a Building When you send a Worker to a Building, if the total Resources of all the Workers you have sent to that Building now equal or exceed the requirements for that Building, the Building is Complete. The Workers you had sent there are returned to you, available for future actions. You receive the coin and point rewards indicated on the Building card. Machines : Machines are special types of Buildings. They do not grant you coins. Instead, when they are completed, they can be treated as a worker and sent to work, at no coin cost. End of the game If you end your turn with 17 or more points on your completed Buildings (and machines), the game will end. community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] While there is something interesting about having workers with different capabilities, my god is this game dry and miserable. I guess it's sort of like Splendor, but imagine Splendor where you have an action economy to assign gems and gems are actually multi gems. Then you have loans and prisoners - ugh. Why subject yourself to this exercise? Value is already very easy to discern in Splendor, and that game already suffers from analysis. Why this? I need to do some linear optimization or something to play well. Not for me.

[Rating: 3/10] It bogs down considerably as players are trying to optimize their actions and the extra actions they can buy. It's a kind of optimization/accounting i'm less eager to do nowadays and especially for a game i consider light. It's a game i would only play with 2 because of the downtime with more players but at the same time there are so many better games for 2.

[Rating: 3/10] Je n'aime pas vraiment la version moyen-âge, mais elle avait le mérite d'être super rapide à expliquer, les règles étant très simples. Mais là, la complexification de presque toutes les phrases rend le jeu assez imbattable. Il n'a pas grand intérêt à mes yeux.

[Rating: 3/10] I simply don't like the iconography or basic mechanic of the The Builder series. I feel like I'm just working on solving a Turing complete problem.

[Rating: 3/10] Ok filler card game where you recruit workers, build buildings whilst managing your money.  Easy to understand but quite linear, recruiting the master craftsmen is the best path and given random market draw luck will decide that.  There are some large point buildings in this version (the Wonders) which is good along with loans and tools.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Not a fan of this game - just using and purchasing cards to build stuff. I don't need to play this again because there are so many other games I'd rather play.

[Rating: 4/10] If a multiplayer solitaire game is going to have appeal to me, actions need to be either somewhat simultaneous are at least quick and smooth.  But this game bogs down in AP and hence the playing time is much too long for a game of this weight.  This game often gets compared to Splendor.  I would take Splendor over this any day.

[Rating: 4/10] Le format de cette petite boîte en métal est pratique pour le voyage. Le jeu est simplissime. Après quelques parties, j'ai l'impression d'en avoir fait le tour. Il n'y a pas (ou très peu) d'interaction avec les autres joueurs et on a l'impression de juste avoir à gérer son argent et construire ses bâtiments.  Les plus : - format de voyage - bien pour initier aux jeux de gestion  Les moins : - pas d'interaction avec les autres joueurs - mécanique de jeu simple
